new.n: Half Moon Lake toboggan slide, Rod & Gun Club park (1917, 1933)
new.pl: Rod & Gun Park, west shore of Half Moon Lake
new.v: Coins, tokens, skate keys, lost jewelry
new.st: By February 1917 a toboggan slide stood at Half Moon Lake, and sleds shot across the ice and up the far hill (Eau Claire Leader, 22 Feb 1917, p. 4). In December 1933 the Rod & Gun Club built a 300-ft slide, 80 to 100 ft high, in "the northeast part of the club's park on the lake", with runs going completely across Half Moon Lake (Eau Claire Leader, 14 Dec 1933, p. 5). The same 1933 item lists the city rink and warming house on Half Moon Lake, the Boyd Park rink, a rink on the vacant lot next to the State Teachers' College, the Mt. Simon kitten-ball field and the Second Ave tennis courts.
new.t: Winter crowds stood at the top and bottom of the slide, and anything dropped on the ice landed on the lake bottom or the far shore when it thawed. The pin is on the northeast part of Rod & Gun Park; the hilltop launch and the shoreline below it are the targets. City park, under the existing City Parks OK.
src: Eau Claire Leader, 22 Feb 1917, p. 4 (newspapers.com image 239465246)
Eau Claire Leader, 14 Dec 1933, p. 5 (newspapers.com image 267195807)
pinev: Two newspaper sources (1917, 1933) put the slide at Half Moon Lake; the 1933 item puts it in the northeast part of the Rod & Gun Club park. Pin on the NE part of Rod & Gun Park (pk-3150); launch spot not mapped, good to about 150 m

ld-mt-washington.st: In November 1921 the wooden scaffold and a 20-ft jump were rebuilt (Eau Claire Leader, 27 Nov 1921, p. 7). The Leader reports ski meets here at least 65 times between 1920 and 1947.
src: Eau Claire Leader, 27 Nov 1921, p. 7 (newspapers.com image 298964214)
